title: Fugue in B minor
blurb: Only one of the nine entries is exact: two are tonal answers and six are altered.
card: Last fugue in Book II, and it ends the collection in a hurry: three voices, 3/8, nine entries in a hundred bars.
history: The subject runs nearly six bars, which in 3/8 is not much clock time but is a lot of fugue: nine statements and eight episodes fill the whole hundred bars. Six of the nine are altered rather than transposed intact — Bach keeps bending intervals inside the subject to fit the harmony he happens to be in. The last entry starts at bar 82 and is finished by bar 88; the thirteen bars after it never touch the subject again.

Book I finishes with a slow, chromatic, four-voice B minor fugue. Book II finishes with this one: quick, three voices, in dance metre. They make an odd pair of bookends, and whether the contrast was deliberate is not something the sources settle.

Book II was put together in Leipzig around 1739–42, nearly twenty years after Book I, out of pieces Bach had been writing over a much longer span. The main source is the London autograph in the British Library, some of it in his hand, some in Anna Magdalena's.
